description.when: Use when the governing exemption law provides both category-specific exemptions and an independently applicable general or wildcard monetary exemption, including 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b), 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123, or 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5).
description.repair: For each owned asset, create an exemption checklist before constructing the output array. First decide whether every applicable general or wildcard exemption can protect any equity; if so, record it unless the allowance is affirmatively exhausted. Then add every category-specific exemption whose complete statutory and factual conditions are established. Never treat a specific exemption, or failure of a specialized test, as displacing a general exemption. Distinguish 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5), the wildcard, from category-specific provisions such as § 522(d)(3). Treat monetary caps as limits on protected value unless the statute expressly makes value an eligibility condition. Apply ordinary category boundaries: wearing apparel requires an actual garment, and a prescribed health aid requires evidence of professional prescription. Before submission, reconcile every asset array against the checklist and reject any array lacking an explicit decision on each applicable general or wildcard exemption.
description.avoid_when: Do not list provisions that only define terms, impose limitations, or govern exemption elections without independently protecting property. Do not apply an exemption when ownership or another express condition fails, no protectable equity exists, or the available allowance is affirmatively exhausted. Do not stretch wearing apparel to jewelry or other adornment, infer a professional prescription without evidence, or substitute a category-specific provision for the applicable wildcard.

description.when: Use when the governing exemption law provides both category-specific exemptions and a general or wildcard monetary exemption that may independently protect the same asset.
description.repair: Evaluate each owned asset independently in two passes. First, record every category-specific exemption whose statutory and factual conditions are satisfied. Second, separately test each applicable general or wildcard exemption and include it whenever it can protect some equity and its allowance is not established as exhausted. A specific exemption does not displace an independently applicable general exemption, and failure of a specialized test does not defeat the general exemption. Treat monetary caps as limits on protected value unless the statute expressly makes value an eligibility condition. Before submission, audit every asset for a documented decision under each independently applicable exemption.
description.avoid_when: Do not list provisions that merely define terms, impose limits, or govern elections without independently protecting property. Do not apply an exemption when an express condition fails, no protectable equity exists, or the available allowance is established as exhausted.
